column3: NASB follows the critical text (“pour out the seven bowls”).
NASB follows the critical text (“into the earth”); it supplies “angel,” and renders “a sore harm and grievous” as “a loathsome and malignant sore.”
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “the second.” NASB follows the critical text (“every living thing”).
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus; it follows the critical text in the rest of the verse.
NASB follows the critical text, without “O Lord” and “and,” rendering “O Holy One” as a title.
NASB follows the critical text (“You have given”); “worthy they are” is rendered “They deserve it.”
NASB follows the critical text (“I heard the altar”).
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus.
NASB follows the critical text; “denigrated” is rendered “blasphemed,” and NASB adds “so as.”
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus; “distress” is rendered “pain.”
“Distresses” is rendered “pains,” and “works” “deeds.”
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus; “the rising of the sun” is rendered “the east.”
NASB follows the critical text (“like frogs”).
NASB follows the critical text (“the kings of the whole world,” “the war”); it omits “that.”
NASB puts the verse in parentheses and quotation marks; “watching” is rendered “stays awake,” and NASB supplies “men.”
NASB spells the name “Har-magedon.”
NASB has “angel,” as in the Textus Receptus; it follows the critical text (“out of the temple from the throne”).
NASB follows the critical text (“since man came to be”); “voices” is rendered “sounds.”
“The wine of the fury of His wrath” is rendered “the wine of His fierce wrath.”
NASB supplies “the.”
“A great hail about a talent in weight” is rendered “huge hailstones, about one hundred pounds each.”
